clue.text: The only way to win in court?

definitions.text: The only way to win in court?

parts.words: The only way to win in court?
parts.note: the court is a tennis court, and a player wins the contest only on taking the final point of the final game and set

explanation.surface: A litigant wonders what it takes to win a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court, where the umpire's call at the winning point ends the contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The umpire's phrase announcing that the final tennis point has decided the whole contest.

clue.text: More colourful environmentalist

definitions.meaning: comparative of green, so having more of a verdant colour
a Green is a member or supporter of an ecological party; the comparative works as more eco-minded

explanation.surface: An eco-campaigner is described as livelier than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads 'environmentalist' as a comparative, someone even more eco-conscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of green in both its colour sense and its ecological, eco-friendly sense.

clue.text: Note going up or down

indicators.note: in a down clue the word reads the same whether the solver goes up the column or down it

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A musical note that rises or falls in pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going up or down' looks like pitch, but it says the word is a palindrome, read either way in the column.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note value, a half note in American usage.

clue.text: Moderate head displays serenity

parts.note: sober means moderate or restrained
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A temperate leader shows calmness.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour place-names; 'displays' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriety of manner shades into calm composure, a sedate seriousness.

clue.text: Handled hazardous trade in tellurium

indicators.note: in places the chemical symbol among the rearranged letters of trade
hazardous suggests letters thrown about by risk, so the word trade is rearranged

parts.note: Te is the chemical symbol for tellurium

explanation.surface: Someone dealt with a dangerous business in a rare element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazardous' turns TRADE into TREAD, and 'in' brings the symbol TE into it, between TREA and D.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat something is to deal with or handle it.

clue.text: Animal turns up possessing strong facial feature

indicators.note: possessing means the reversed animal holds the abbreviation inside it
in a down clue turning up means the word for the animal is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lion is an animal

explanation.surface: A beast appears with a powerful part of its face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal turns up' reads like a creature appearing; in a down clue 'turns up' means read upwards, and 'possessing' sets the abbreviation within the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is one of the nose's openings, a feature of the face.

clue.text: Dotty copper dashes away signalling in code

definitions.text: Dotty copper dashes away signalling in code

parts.words: Dotty copper dashes away signalling in code
parts.note: a fictional Oxford detective shares his name with the telegraph system of dots and dashes

explanation.surface: A dizzy policeman rushes off, sending coded signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a famous TV detective; 'dotty' and 'dashes' are both the code's symbols and a crazy, hurrying policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: The telegraphic code of dots and dashes is named after its inventor, also a fictional detective inspector.

clue.text: Art in line to be displayed every three years

indicators.note: displayed suggests set out afresh, so the letters of art in line are rearranged

explanation.surface: Artworks in a row are shown at a recurring exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be displayed' rearranges ART IN LINE; the surface hints at a triennial art show.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial describes something recurring at three-year intervals.

clue.text: Observing that he would listen with a gin sling

indicators.note: listen tells the solver to hear the contraction spoken rather than read it

parts.note: he would contracts to he'd, said like heed

indicators.note: a sling is a mixed drink, so the word gin is mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone notices a man would enjoy a mixed gin drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listen' turns HE'D into the sound HEED; 'sling' mixes GIN into ING. A gin sling is a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying attention to something means observing or minding it.

clue.text: Elevate to part of Aberdeen? No, Bletchley park

indicators.note: part of says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Raising someone to a Scottish city is rejected in favour of a famous codebreaking site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' shows the letters run across aberdeEN NO BLEtchley; Bletchley Park was Britain's wartime codebreaking centre.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise someone to the peerage is to elevate them in rank.

clue.text: Submissive minister hosts international league

indicators.note: hosts means the verb for minister takes the abbreviations in

parts.note: to minister to is to serve

explanation.surface: A meek government minister welcomes an international sports league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun but is the verb to serve; 'hosts' puts I and L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Servile means fawningly obedient, like a servant.

clue.text: The one in one over two

definitions.text: The one in one over two

parts.words: The one in one over two
parts.note: in the fraction a half, written as one over two, the upper figure is the one

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which digit is the one in one over two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over two' reads like cricket or a score but is the fraction 1/2.
explanation.definitionFit: The top part of a fraction, above the line, is named for counting the parts.

clue.text: Weariness caused by regularly lean insulin

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words lean insulin

explanation.surface: Fatigue blamed on a slim dose of insulin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' picks the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th letters of LEAN INSULIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom or weariness of spirit.

clue.text: He'd read about the pochard, for instance

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of he'd read are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reads up on the pochard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' rearranges HE'D READ. The redhead is a North American duck closely related to the pochard.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck known as the redhead belongs to the pochard group of diving ducks.

clue.text: Spoke after declaration of having done some DIY

indicators.note: after says the verb for spoke comes behind the abbreviation for declaration

parts.note: dec. is the cricket abbreviation for declared or declaration
orated means spoke formally

explanation.surface: Someone talks after announcing they have done home improvements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' could be a wheel part; it is ORATED, put 'after' DEC, the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting or wallpapering a room is a home improvement job.

clue.text: Tendency for fish to give birth internally

indicators.note: internally means the verb for giving birth goes inside the fish

parts.note: the ling is a long-bodied sea fish
ean is an old word meaning to give birth, used of ewes

explanation.surface: A habit of fish to bear young inside the body.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb meaning to give birth is an archaic farming word for lambing, and 'internally' puts it inside the fish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaning is an inclination or bias toward something.

clue.text: Drunkenly laces a gin producing painlessness

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests reeling about, so the letters of laces a gin are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone tipsily spikes a gin to dull the pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunkenly' rearranges LACES A GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkilling drug relieves pain without loss of consciousness.

clue.text: Speaks first to moneyman returning expenses

indicators.note: returning means the accountant's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant, a man handling money
costs are expenses

explanation.surface: An accountant comes back with the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' reverses CA, a chartered accountant, to AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To accost someone is to approach and address them first, often boldly.

clue.text: Fool, for example, given first-class weapon

parts.note: an ass is a fool
A1 means first-class, with the figure one read as letter I

explanation.surface: An idiot is handed a top-quality arm.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, meaning top-rate, is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Relative takes short walk to meet another relative

parts.note: a step is a very short walk
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member strolls briefly to meet another family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' and 'to meet' join the definition to the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's child from an earlier marriage is a family connection by marriage.

clue.text: Drink tea — blissful by half!

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

indicators.note: by half means only the first half of the word blissful is used

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to drink tea, a half-measure of bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By half' takes the first four of BLISSFUL's eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chablis is a dry white wine from Burgundy.

clue.text: Hear cad deciphered a riddle

indicators.note: deciphered suggests letters being worked out of a code into new order, so hear cad is rearranged

explanation.surface: A rogue is heard solving a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deciphered' rearranges HEAR CAD.
explanation.definitionFit: In a charade, a word is guessed from clues to its syllables, a kind of riddle.

clue.text: Fashionable world of fellowship

definitions.meaning: an association or club of members

explanation.surface: The smart set described as a companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the elite social set and an organised association of members.

clue.text: Selects specimens

definitions.meaning: kinds or types, examples of a class

explanation.surface: Someone chooses samples.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means picks or classifies; as a plural noun, kinds or examples of a type.

clue.text: Excessive footprint on earth

indicators.note: on here means the footprint is placed over earth, enclosing it

parts.note: a step can mean a footprint or footstep

explanation.surface: An outsize impression left on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: E for earth goes inside STEP; 'on' is read as STEP fitting around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Steep prices are unreasonably high or excessive.

clue.text: Protestant messenger found in English vicarage

indicators.note: found in means the messenger sits within the shortened vicarage

parts.note: vic is a short form taken from vicar and vicarage
an angel is a divine messenger

explanation.surface: A Protestant herald turns up at the English vicar's home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found in' places the heavenly messenger within the clipped form of vicarage, with the abbreviation for English leading.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangelic describes Protestant churches stressing the gospel and personal conversion.

clue.text: Loch dried out soundly by landowner

indicators.note: soundly means the letters assembled are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: L abbreviates loch and arid means dried out, together said like the Scots landowner

explanation.surface: A Scottish lake parched completely, near the estate's owner.
explanation.walkthrough: L (loch) plus ARID, said aloud, sounds like the word. A laird is a Scottish landowner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is the Scots term for the owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Understands that the gun he started reloading, stuck

parts.note: gat is slang for a gun

indicators.note: started means the first letters of reloading and stuck are taken

explanation.surface: Someone realises that a gunman's weapon jammed while being reloaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Started' picks R and S, the first letters of 'reloading' and 'stuck'; 'that the' joins the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather something can mean to infer or understand it.

clue.text: Loose scabs, ie, fall off

indicators.note: loose suggests the letters are set free and come away in a new order

explanation.surface: Wounds heal as loosened scabs drop away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' rearranges SCABS IE.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, abscission is a leaf or fruit separating and dropping from the plant.

clue.text: Self-governing time in July

parts.note: the American holiday on the fourth of July marks the colonies becoming self-governing

explanation.surface: A summer date celebrating national autonomy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fourth of July holiday celebrates America's 1776 declaration breaking from British rule.
